eras.title: the beginning
eras.summary: the universe begins, stars forge the elements, the earth forms, life appears in the sea, and over billions of years it grows into fish, forests, dinosaurs, and mammals.

eras.title: the first humans
eras.summary: in africa, apes begin walking upright. their descendants make tools, tame fire, and develop language. our own species spreads across every continent but antarctica, outliving all other kinds of human.

eras.title: the first farmers
eras.summary: as the ice age ends, people in at least seven parts of the world start farming on their own. villages, pottery, property, and new diseases follow, and the population of the world begins to climb.

eras.title: the first civilizations
eras.summary: cities, kings, writing, law, and organized war appear along the great rivers of mesopotamia, egypt, the indus, and china, and on their own in the americas. the bronze age ends in a sudden collapse.

eras.title: the classical world
eras.summary: persia, greece, rome, the mauryas, the guptas, the qin, and the han build vast empires. philosophers and prophets ask questions that are still argued about, and the silk roads link east and west.

eras.title: the middle ages
eras.summary: the western roman empire falls, islam spreads across three continents, tang and song china lead the world in technology, the mongols conquer most of eurasia, and the black death kills a third of europe.

eras.title: the early modern world
eras.summary: the printing press, ocean voyages, and the conquest of the americas tie the whole world together for the first time, through trade, disease, and slavery. the reformation splits europe and science is reborn.

eras.title: the age of revolutions
eras.summary: enlightenment ideas about rights and reason fuel revolutions in america, france, haiti, and latin america, while steam power and factories begin the industrial revolution in britain.

eras.title: industry and empire
eras.summary: railways, steel, electricity, and the telegraph remake daily life. industrial nations use their new power to seize most of africa and much of asia, while new ideas like nationalism and socialism spread.

eras.title: the world wars
eras.summary: two world wars, the russian revolution, the great depression, and the rise of fascism make this the deadliest stretch in human history, ending with the holocaust and the atomic bomb.

eras.title: the modern world
eras.summary: the cold war, the end of empires, the struggle for civil rights, space flight, the computer, and the internet shape the world we live in now, along with new dangers like climate change.

events.text: the big bang: space, time, matter, and energy begin expanding from an extremely hot, dense state
about 380,000 years after the big bang, the first atoms form and light travels freely for the first time; it survives today as the cosmic microwave background
the first stars ignite, made almost entirely of hydrogen and helium
early galaxies take shape, including the oldest parts of our own milky way
a cloud of gas and dust, enriched by the remains of earlier stars, collapses to form the sun and a disk of material around it
the earth forms as rock and dust in the young solar system clump together
a mars-sized body, often called theia, strikes the young earth; the debris forms the moon
the oldest known mineral crystals on earth form; zircons later found in western australia hint that liquid water already existed
the earliest likely traces of life: chemical signs of microbes preserved in ancient rocks
microbial mats build stromatolites, layered rock mounds that are among the oldest clear fossils, found in western australia
the great oxidation event: oxygen made by photosynthesizing cyanobacteria begins to build up in the air
complex cells (eukaryotes) appear, with a nucleus and mitochondria that were once free-living bacteria
the first known multicellular algae, and some of the earliest evidence of sexual reproduction
"snowball earth": ice spreads close to the equator in one of the most extreme cold periods in the planet's history
the ediacaran biota: strange soft-bodied creatures, among the first large complex organisms, live on the sea floor
the cambrian explosion begins: most major animal groups appear within a few tens of millions of years
simple plants related to mosses begin to colonize the land
the end-ordovician extinction, caused by a sharp ice age, wipes out most species in the sea
tiktaalik, a fish with sturdy limb-like fins and a neck, lives in shallow streams; it shows how fish gave rise to land animals
the late devonian extinction devastates reefs and ocean life
vast swamp forests of giant ferns and club mosses cover the land; their buried remains become much of today's coal
the first amniotes, the ancestors of reptiles, birds, and mammals, lay eggs that can survive on dry land
the great dying (permian-triassic extinction), driven by huge volcanic eruptions in siberia, kills about 90 percent of species in the sea
the earliest known dinosaurs, small two-legged hunters, live in what is now argentina and brazil
the first mammal-like animals appear: small, furry, and probably active at night
the end-triassic extinction clears the way for dinosaurs to dominate
the supercontinent pangaea begins to split apart, opening the atlantic ocean
archaeopteryx, a feathered dinosaur that could probably fly, lives in what is now germany
the first flowering plants appear, and later spread alongside pollinating insects
an asteroid about ten kilometers wide hits chicxulub in mexico; all non-bird dinosaurs die out along with about three quarters of all species
a sudden hot spell warms the planet; early primates, horses, and many other mammal groups spread widely
india crashes into asia, beginning the rise of the himalayas
permanent ice sheets begin to form on antarctica as the planet cools
the ancestors of apes split from old world monkeys
the lineage leading to humans separates from the one leading to chimpanzees; sahelanthropus in chad may be one of the earliest members
ardipithecus ("ardi") in ethiopia walks upright on the ground but still climbs trees with grasping feet
hominins leave a trail of footprints in volcanic ash at laetoli, tanzania, proving they walked fully upright
the oldest known stone tools are made at lomekwi, kenya, before our own genus existed
"lucy", an australopithecus afarensis, lives and dies in the afar region of ethiopia
the earliest known fossil of our genus, homo, a jawbone from ledi-geraru, ethiopia
the pleistocene ice ages begin: dozens of cycles of cold glacial and warmer periods
oldowan stone tools, simple sharp flakes, become common in east africa
homo erectus appears, with a body much like ours and a larger brain
early humans reach dmanisi in the caucasus of georgia, among the first to leave africa
acheulean hand axes, carefully shaped teardrop tools, are made; the design lasts over a million years
homo erectus lives on java, in what is now indonesia
burned bone and ash in wonderwerk cave, south africa, are some of the earliest evidence of fire use
hearths at gesher benot ya'aqov in israel show humans controlling fire repeatedly
at sima de los huesos in spain, early ancestors of the neanderthals leave their remains in a deep cave pit
the oldest known fossils of homo sapiens, our own species, from jebel irhoud, morocco
early homo sapiens live for a time at skhul and qafzeh in israel, then seem to disappear from the region
people at blombos cave, south africa, engrave patterns on red ochre and make shell beads: early signs of symbolic thought
the toba supervolcano on sumatra erupts, the largest eruption of the last two million years
people may have reached australia by now, crossing open sea by boat; the ancestors of aboriginal australians
the main migration of homo sapiens out of africa begins; nearly everyone outside africa today descends from it
a painting of a wild pig and people on a cave wall on sulawesi, indonesia, the oldest known picture of a scene
homo sapiens arrive in europe, where neanderthals already live
the neanderthals die out; many people today carry a small share of their dna
the lion man of hohlenstein-stadel, a half-lion half-human ivory figure, and bone flutes are made in germany
artists paint lions, rhinos, and horses on the walls of chauvet cave in france
human footprints at white sands, new mexico, show people in the americas during the height of the ice age
the last glacial maximum: ice sheets are at their largest and sea levels about 120 meters lower than today
the painted caves of lascaux in france are decorated with hundreds of animals
dogs, descended from wolves, are firmly established as human companions, the first tamed animal
people live at monte verde in southern chile, far down the americas
the clovis culture spreads across north america, famous for its fluted stone spear points
the younger dryas: a sudden return to near ice-age cold that lasts about 1,200 years
many large animals, including mammoths, giant ground sloths, and woolly rhinos, have died out, likely from climate change and hunting
the younger dryas ends and the holocene begins: a warm, stable climate that has lasted to today
göbekli tepe in southern turkey: huge carved stone pillars raised by hunter-gatherers, the oldest known monumental site
wheat, barley, lentils, and peas are domesticated in the fertile crescent
sheep and goats are domesticated in the zagros mountains and nearby
cattle are tamed from the wild aurochs, both in the near east and separately in south asia
jericho is surrounded by a stone wall with a great tower, one of the oldest town walls known
millet is farmed in northern china, along the yellow river
squash is domesticated in mexico
çatalhöyük in anatolia grows into a crowded town of mud-brick houses entered through the roof
rice is domesticated in the lower yangtze valley of china
farmers at mehrgarh, in modern pakistan, grow barley and wheat and keep cattle
farmers in the highlands of new guinea dig drainage ditches to grow taro and bananas
maize begins to be domesticated from a wild grass called teosinte in southern mexico
people at jiahu in china brew a fermented drink of rice, honey, and fruit, and play bone flutes
farming spreads from anatolia into greece and the balkans, carried by migrating farmers
potatoes, quinoa, and beans are being domesticated in the andes
farmers in mesopotamia dig irrigation canals to water fields with river water
during the "green sahara", herders graze cattle across lands that are now desert, and paint them on rocks
copper is smelted from ore in the balkans and iran, beginning the copper age
farming with barley, wheat, and cattle is established along the nile
the varna cemetery in bulgaria holds the oldest worked gold known, buried with a few very rich people
people in brittany, france, raise thousands of standing stones at carnac
the plow pulled by oxen lets farmers work much more land
the sahara begins drying out; herders move toward the nile and the savanna
farmers build large wooden and stone tombs across britain and ireland
the botai people of kazakhstan use horses, perhaps riding and milking them
the wheel appears in mesopotamia and central europe at almost the same time
llamas and alpacas are domesticated in the andes
uruk in southern mesopotamia grows into perhaps the first true city, with tens of thousands of people and huge temples
the bronze age begins in the near east as smiths alloy copper with arsenic and later tin
ötzi the iceman dies in the alps; his frozen body, clothes, and copper axe survive to modern times
writing is invented in sumer: first as tallies and pictures on clay for keeping accounts, later as cuneiform
egyptian hieroglyphs appear, possibly invented independently of mesopotamian writing
upper and lower egypt are united under one king, remembered as narmer or menes
the first stage of stonehenge, a circular ditch and bank, is dug in southern britain
austronesian-speaking peoples begin sailing out of taiwan, starting a migration that will reach madagascar and easter island
the architect imhotep builds the step pyramid of djoser at saqqara, the first large building made entirely of stone
the harappan cities of the indus valley, like harappa and mohenjo-daro, reach their height, with grid streets and covered drains
caral in peru's supe valley builds pyramids and sunken plazas, the oldest city in the americas
the great pyramid of giza is completed for the pharaoh khufu; it stays the tallest human-made structure for nearly 4,000 years
kerma, the first kingdom of kush, flourishes on the nile in what is now sudan
the indus cities use short written signs on stamp seals and a standard set of stone weights; the script has never been deciphered
sargon of akkad conquers the sumerian cities and builds what is often called the first empire
ur-nammu of ur issues the oldest surviving law code; the first poems about gilgamesh are written down
minoan palaces rise on crete, centered on knossos
people of the sintashta culture on the steppe build light chariots with spoked wheels
people in eastern north america domesticate squash, sunflowers, and other seed plants
the indus cities go into decline as rivers shift and the climate dries
semitic-speaking workers in egypt scratch the earliest known alphabet onto rocks in sinai and the western desert
babylonian scribes do advanced mathematics in base sixty; we still use it for 60 minutes and 360 degrees
hammurabi of babylon has 282 laws carved on a stone pillar, the famous code of hammurabi
the shang dynasty takes power along the yellow river, the first chinese dynasty with written records
the volcano of thera (santorini) erupts in one of the largest blasts in human history; mycenaean greece begins to rise
indo-aryan speaking peoples settle in northern india; the rigveda, oldest of the vedas, is composed
hatshepsut rules egypt as pharaoh, sending trade expeditions to the land of punt
mycenaean greeks take over knossos and write an early form of greek in the script called linear b
akhenaten becomes pharaoh and orders egypt to worship only the sun disk, the aten
the hittite empire of anatolia is at the height of its power
the young pharaoh tutankhamun dies; his tomb is found almost untouched in 1922
lapita peoples sail from the islands off new guinea into the remote pacific, reaching fiji, tonga, and samoa
egypt under ramesses ii and the hittites fight the battle of kadesh; later they sign one of the oldest known peace treaties
shang kings carve questions to their ancestors on oracle bones, the oldest chinese writing
the olmec civilization rises on the gulf coast of mexico, carving colossal stone heads
ironworking spreads across the region, starting the iron age
the bronze age collapse: the hittite empire, mycenaean greece, and many cities of the eastern mediterranean fall
ramesses iii fights off the "sea peoples" in the nile delta, but egypt is left weakened
the phoenicians use an alphabet of 22 letters, the ancestor of the greek, latin, hebrew, and arabic scripts
the zhou overthrow the shang and claim the "mandate of heaven"
david rules a kingdom of israel from jerusalem; his son solomon is said to build the first temple
bantu-speaking farmers begin spreading south and east from west-central africa, carrying farming and later iron
the temple center of chavín de huántar spreads a shared religion and art style through the andes
phoenicians from tyre found carthage in north africa, according to tradition
the first recorded olympic games are held at olympia in greece, according to later tradition
the legendary founding of rome by romulus
the greeks adopt the phoenician alphabet, adding vowels; the iliad and the odyssey take shape
kushite kings from nubia conquer egypt and rule it as its 25th dynasty
the assyrian empire destroys the northern kingdom of israel and deports much of its population
babylonians and medes sack nineveh, and the assyrian empire collapses
the kingdom of lydia in anatolia strikes the first coins, lumps of electrum stamped with a lion's head
babylon destroys jerusalem and its temple; many judeans are exiled to babylon
confucius is born in the state of lu, according to tradition
cyrus the great founds the achaemenid persian empire
cyrus takes babylon and allows the exiled jews to return and rebuild their temple
the romans expel their last king and found the republic, by tradition
cleisthenes reforms athens, laying the foundations of democracy
the nok culture of nigeria smelts iron and makes striking terracotta sculptures
the dong son culture of northern vietnam casts large bronze drums that are traded across southeast asia
siddhartha gautama, the buddha, teaches in northern india; mahavira teaches jainism in the same region (the exact dates are debated)
athens defeats a persian invasion at the battle of marathon
the spartans make their stand at thermopylae, and the greek fleet wins at salamis
the warring states period: rival chinese kingdoms fight for supremacy while philosophy flourishes
the parthenon is built on the acropolis of athens
the peloponnesian war between athens and sparta ends in athens' defeat
hippocrates and his followers teach that illnesses have natural causes, not punishments from the gods
socrates is tried in athens and put to death by drinking hemlock
alexander the great conquers the persian empire and marches to india
alexander dies in babylon at 32; his generals split his empire
chandragupta maurya founds the maurya empire, the first to unite most of india
meroë becomes the capital of kush, a center of iron smelting with its own steep pyramids
the library of alexandria is founded in egypt under the ptolemies
euclid writes the elements in alexandria, a textbook of geometry used for more than two thousand years
the three punic wars between rome and carthage end with carthage destroyed
ashoka conquers kalinga, is horrified by the slaughter, and turns to buddhism and non-violence
eratosthenes measures the size of the earth using the shadows cast in two egyptian cities
the king of qin conquers the last rival state and becomes qin shi huang, the first emperor of china
hannibal of carthage crosses the alps into italy with an army and war elephants
modu chanyu unites the xiongnu nomads of the mongolian steppe into an empire strong enough to make the han pay tribute
the han dynasty begins; it will rule china for about four centuries
the nazca people of peru draw giant lines and animal figures across the desert
after the travels of the han envoy zhang qian, the trade routes later called the silk roads open between china and the west
the hopewell culture builds large earthworks and trades across much of eastern north america
julius caesar is assassinated by senators in rome
octavian takes the name augustus and becomes the first roman emperor; the pax romana begins
jesus of nazareth is born in judea
the kingdom of funan grows rich in the mekong delta, trading between india and china
jesus is crucified in jerusalem; his followers begin to spread christianity
the romans crush a jewish revolt and destroy the second temple in jerusalem
mount vesuvius erupts and buries pompeii and herculaneum
the moche culture on peru's north coast builds adobe pyramids and makes fine portrait pottery
the kingdom of aksum in ethiopia and eritrea grows rich on red sea trade
the court official cai lun presents an improved method of making paper
the roman empire reaches its largest size under the emperor trajan
zhang heng builds a bronze seismoscope that shows the direction of a distant earthquake
the greek doctor galen begins working in rome; his books on medicine are followed for over a thousand years
the antonine plague, probably smallpox, spreads through the roman empire and kills millions
teotihuacan in central mexico, with its pyramid of the sun, becomes one of the largest cities in the world
the han dynasty falls and china splits into three kingdoms
the sasanian persian empire is founded; it will rival rome for four centuries
the classic period of the maya begins, with great cities like tikal and calakmul
the edict of milan ends the persecution of christians in the roman empire
chandragupta i founds the gupta empire; a golden age of science, math, and art follows
constantine makes byzantium, renamed constantinople, the new capital of the empire
king ezana of aksum converts to christianity
christianity becomes the official religion of the roman empire
the roman empire is permanently divided into eastern and western halves
the visigoths under alaric sack the city of rome
the germanic general odoacer deposes romulus augustulus, the last western roman emperor
justinian rules the byzantine empire, reconquers italy and north africa, and codifies roman law
the hagia sophia is completed in constantinople, the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years
the plague of justinian, the first known pandemic of bubonic plague, strikes the mediterranean world
muhammad is born in mecca
the sui dynasty reunites china after centuries of division and builds the grand canal
muhammad begins receiving the revelations that become the quran, according to muslim tradition
the tang dynasty begins, a golden age of poetry, trade, and buddhism
the hijra: muhammad and his followers move from mecca to medina, year one of the islamic calendar
the monk xuanzang travels from china to india along the silk roads and returns with hundreds of buddhist texts
muhammad dies; abu bakr becomes the first caliph
arab muslim armies conquer the sasanian empire, syria, egypt, north africa, and spain
srivijaya, a trading empire based on sumatra, controls the strait of malacca and becomes a center of buddhist learning
husayn, grandson of muhammad, is killed at karbala, deepening the split between sunni and shia muslims
the empire of ghana, the "land of gold", grows rich on camel caravans carrying gold and salt across the sahara
muslim forces cross into spain and conquer most of the iberian peninsula
the abbasid dynasty overthrows the umayyads and later builds baghdad as its capital
abbasid and tang armies clash at the talas river; papermaking spreads west to the islamic world
vikings raid the monastery of lindisfarne in england, beginning the viking age
the pope crowns charlemagne emperor of the romans
the huge buddhist monument of borobudur is built on java
most of the great classic maya cities of the southern lowlands are abandoned
al-khwarizmi writes his book on algebra at the house of wisdom in baghdad
the diamond sutra is printed in china, the oldest dated printed book
the song dynasty begins; china leads the world in technology, trade, and city life
leif erikson and other norse sailors reach newfoundland, at l'anse aux meadows
polynesian voyagers settle the far corners of the pacific, reaching hawaii and later easter island
ibn al-haytham writes his book of optics in cairo, testing ideas about light and sight with careful experiments
the song government issues the jiaozi in sichuan, the world's first official paper money
ibn sina (avicenna) completes the canon of medicine, used in europe and the islamic world for centuries
bi sheng invents movable type made of baked clay
a chinese military handbook records the earliest known formula for gunpowder
cahokia near the mississippi river grows into the largest city north of mexico, with huge earthen mounds
the great schism: the catholic and orthodox churches formally split
william of normandy wins the battle of hastings and conquers england
the university of bologna is founded, the oldest in continuous operation in europe
the first crusade captures jerusalem and massacres many of its people
the khmer king suryavarman ii builds angkor wat, the largest religious monument in the world
saladin defeats the crusaders at hattin and retakes jerusalem
king lalibela of ethiopia has churches carved down into solid rock
swahili trading cities like kilwa and mombasa prosper on indian ocean trade
polynesian voyagers reach rapa nui (easter island), where their descendants carve the giant moai statues
temüjin unites the mongol tribes and is proclaimed genghis khan
the delhi sultanate is founded by turkic muslim rulers in northern india
english barons force king john to agree to the magna carta
sundiata keita defeats the sosso and founds the mali empire
the ancestors of the māori, sailing from eastern polynesia, settle new zealand, the last large land mass humans reached
ancestral puebloans build cliff dwellings at mesa verde in colorado; by 1300 they have moved away
the thule people, ancestors of the inuit, spread east across arctic canada to greenland, hunting whales from skin boats
the mongols sack baghdad and end the abbasid caliphate
marco polo travels to china and serves at the court of kublai khan
two mongol invasions of japan are wrecked by typhoons, the "kamikaze" or divine winds
kublai khan completes the conquest of the song; the mongol yuan dynasty rules all of china
osman i founds the small anatolian state that becomes the ottoman empire
great zimbabwe, with its huge dry-stone walls, is at the height of its power
mansa musa of mali makes his pilgrimage to mecca, spending so much gold in cairo that its value falls
the mexica (aztecs) found tenochtitlan on an island in lake texcoco
ibn battuta travels about 120,000 kilometers through the islamic world and beyond, from west africa to china
the hundred years' war between england and france
the black death kills roughly a third to a half of europe's people; it also ravages the middle east and north africa
the majapahit empire, based on java, reaches its height and claims much of modern indonesia
the ming dynasty drives out the mongols and rules china
timur conquers an empire from his capital at samarkand, from anatolia to india, at a terrible cost in lives
the kingdom of kongo takes shape south of the congo river
admiral zheng he leads seven giant treasure fleets as far as east africa
joan of arc leads the french to lift the siege of orléans
pachacuti becomes ruler of the inca and begins their rapid expansion
king sejong of korea has hangul created, a simple alphabet for the korean language
johannes gutenberg builds a printing press with movable metal type in mainz
the ottomans under mehmed ii capture constantinople, ending the byzantine empire
sonni ali builds the songhai empire along the niger river, taking timbuktu and djenné
bartolomeu dias sails around the southern tip of africa
christopher columbus, sailing for spain, reaches the caribbean
granada, the last muslim state in spain, falls; spain expels its jews
vasco da gama reaches calicut in india by sailing around africa
guru nanak begins teaching in the punjab; his followers become the sikhs
ismail i founds the safavid empire in persia and makes shia islam the state religion
the transatlantic slave trade carries about 12.5 million africans in chains to the americas; nearly 2 million die at sea
leonardo da vinci begins painting the mona lisa
michelangelo paints the ceiling of the sistine chapel
martin luther's 95 theses challenge the catholic church and start the reformation
hernán cortés and indigenous allies conquer the aztec empire; smallpox kills much of tenochtitlan
the expedition begun by ferdinand magellan becomes the first to sail around the world
smallpox, brought by the spanish, kills a huge share of the people of tenochtitlan
suleiman the magnificent rules the ottoman empire at its height
babur wins the battle of panipat and founds the mughal empire
the ottomans besiege vienna but fail to take it
francisco pizarro captures and executes the inca ruler atahualpa, and the inca empire falls
henry viii makes himself head of the church of england
copernicus publishes his theory that the earth orbits the sun
silver is found at potosí in bolivia; forced native labor makes it one of the richest mines in history
in the valladolid debate, bartolomé de las casas argues against the enslavement and abuse of the peoples of the americas
akbar the great rules the mughal empire and welcomes debate between religions
spain founds manila; galleons now link the americas and asia, and american silver flows to china
the spanish armada fails to invade england
a moroccan army with guns defeats the songhai empire
japan invades korea; admiral yi sun-sin's navy, with its armored turtle ships, helps drive them back
the english east india company is chartered; the dutch company follows in 1602
tokugawa ieyasu becomes shogun; japan enters over 250 years of peace and isolation
the dutch sailor willem janszoon makes the first recorded european landing in australia
the english found jamestown in virginia
johannes kepler shows that the planets move around the sun in ellipses, not perfect circles
galileo uses a telescope to see the moons of jupiter
the thirty years' war devastates central europe; the peace of westphalia ends it
the first recorded enslaved africans arrive in english virginia
the taj mahal is built by shah jahan as a tomb for his wife mumtaz mahal
abel tasman reaches tasmania and new zealand
the manchus take beijing and found the qing dynasty, china's last
the dutch east india company founds cape town
the kangxi emperor rules qing china for 61 years, one of the longest reigns in history
the great plague of london kills about 100,000 people, nearly a quarter of the city
the pueblo revolt drives spanish colonists out of new mexico for twelve years
peter the great rules russia and forces it to modernize along western lines
the ottomans are defeated at the second siege of vienna
isaac newton publishes the principia, explaining gravity and the laws of motion
the glorious revolution in england limits the power of the crown; a bill of rights follows
the treaty of nerchinsk sets the border between russia and qing china, china's first treaty with a european power
osei tutu founds the asante kingdom in the gold-rich forests of modern ghana, united by the golden stool
thomas newcomen builds the first practical steam engine, to pump water from mines
vitus bering, sailing for russia, reaches alaska
diderot and d'alembert publish the first volume of the encyclopédie
the seven years' war is fought across europe, north america, india, and at sea; britain gains canada and power in india
the east india company wins the battle of plassey and takes control of bengal
rousseau publishes the social contract
catherine the great rules russia, expanding it to the black sea
james cook makes three voyages across the pacific, mapping new zealand and eastern australia
james watt patents a much more efficient steam engine
colonists dump british tea into boston harbor, the boston tea party
the thirteen colonies declare independence from britain
adam smith publishes the wealth of nations
tupac amaru ii leads a great indigenous uprising against spanish rule in peru; it is crushed and he is executed
british forces surrender at yorktown
the united states constitution is written in philadelphia
the british "first fleet" arrives at sydney; the colonization of australia begins
the french revolution begins; a crowd storms the bastille and the declaration of the rights of man is issued
the haitian revolution: enslaved people in saint-domingue rise up and create the free nation of haiti
mary wollstonecraft publishes a vindication of the rights of woman

people.name: lucy
people.about: her partial skeleton, found in ethiopia, showed that human ancestors walked upright long before their brains grew large

people.name: turkana boy
people.about: his nearly complete skeleton, found by lake turkana in kenya, shows a body already built much like ours, tall and made for walking long distances

people.name: denny
people.role: a girl known from a bone fragment in denisova cave, siberia
people.about: her dna showed that her mother was a neanderthal and her father a denisovan, proof that different kinds of humans had children together

people.name: mungo man
people.about: the oldest known human remains in australia, buried with care and sprinkled with red ochre by lake mungo

people.name: ötzi
people.role: a copper age man found frozen in the alps
people.about: his body, clothing, tools, and even stomach contents survived, giving a rare close look at a single prehistoric life

people.name: narmer
people.about: traditionally credited with uniting upper and lower egypt; the narmer palette shows him wearing both crowns

people.name: imhotep
people.about: designed the step pyramid of djoser, the first large building made entirely of stone, and was later worshipped as a god of medicine

people.name: khufu
people.about: the great pyramid of giza was built as his tomb

people.name: sargon of akkad
people.about: conquered the sumerian city-states and created what is often called the first empire

people.name: enheduanna
people.role: high priestess of ur and poet
people.about: the daughter of sargon, she is the earliest author in history known by name

people.name: hammurabi
people.about: built a large kingdom in mesopotamia and published one of the best known early law codes

people.name: hatshepsut
people.about: one of the few women to rule egypt as pharaoh; her reign was peaceful and prosperous, and she built the temple at deir el-bahri

people.name: zoroaster
people.about: founder of zoroastrianism, which saw the world as a struggle between good and evil; his dates are very uncertain

people.name: akhenaten
people.about: tried to replace egypt's many gods with worship of the aten, the sun disk, and built a new capital at amarna

people.name: nefertiti
people.about: wife of akhenaten and a powerful figure in her own right; her painted bust is one of the most famous works of ancient art

people.name: tutankhamun
people.about: a young king who restored the old gods after akhenaten; his nearly intact tomb made him famous

people.name: ramesses ii
people.about: ruled for 66 years, fought the hittites at kadesh, and built huge monuments such as abu simbel

people.name: homer
people.about: the name given to the poet of the iliad and the odyssey; whether one person composed both is debated

people.name: nebuchadnezzar ii
people.about: rebuilt babylon in glazed brick, destroyed jerusalem in 587 bce, and carried many of its people into exile

people.name: sappho
people.role: greek poet from the island of lesbos
people.about: wrote lyric poems about love and longing that the ancients ranked beside homer; only fragments survive

people.name: cyrus the great
people.role: founder of the achaemenid persian empire
people.about: conquered media, lydia, and babylon, and was remembered for letting conquered peoples keep their customs

people.name: laozi
people.about: traditionally the author of the dao de jing and founder of daoism; he may be partly legendary

people.name: mahavira
people.about: taught strict non-violence toward all living things; jains count him as the last of 24 great teachers

people.name: confucius
people.about: taught that a good society rests on proper relationships, respect for family, and rulers who lead by virtue

people.name: darius i
people.about: organized the persian empire into provinces, built roads, and launched the first invasion of greece

people.name: sun tzu
people.about: traditionally credited with the art of war, a short book on strategy still read by soldiers and business people

people.name: pericles
people.about: led athens in its golden age, backed democracy and the building of the parthenon, and died of plague early in the war with sparta

people.name: herodotus
people.about: called the father of history; his histories tell the story of the persian wars and the peoples involved

people.name: siddhartha gautama
people.about: a prince who gave up his wealth to seek an end to suffering and taught the four noble truths and the eightfold path; some date him about 80 years earlier

people.name: socrates
people.about: questioned everything, wrote nothing, and was executed for corrupting the young; we know him through plato

people.name: hippocrates
people.about: taught that diseases have natural causes rather than divine ones; the hippocratic oath is named after him

people.name: plato
people.about: student of socrates, founder of the academy, and author of the republic

people.name: aristotle
people.about: wrote on logic, biology, ethics, politics, and more; teacher of alexander the great

people.name: alexander the great
people.about: conquered the persian empire and reached india by the age of 30, spreading greek culture across the east

people.name: chandragupta maurya
people.about: united most of northern india after alexander's invasion; tradition says he later became a jain monk

people.name: ashoka
people.about: after the bloody conquest of kalinga he embraced buddhism and carved edicts about kindness across his empire

people.name: euclid
people.about: his elements built up geometry from a few simple starting rules and was used as a textbook for over two thousand years

people.name: archimedes
people.about: worked out the principles of levers and buoyancy and estimated pi; killed when rome took syracuse

people.name: eratosthenes
people.role: greek scholar and head of the library of alexandria
people.about: measured the size of the earth from the angle of shadows in two cities and came close to the right answer

people.name: qin shi huang
people.about: united china, standardized writing, money, and measures, and was buried with the terracotta army

people.name: hannibal
people.about: crossed the alps with elephants and crushed roman armies at cannae, but carthage still lost the war

people.name: sima qian
people.about: wrote the records of the grand historian, the model for chinese history writing for two thousand years

people.name: julius caesar
people.about: conquered gaul, won a civil war, and was murdered by senators who feared he would become king

people.name: cleopatra
people.about: allied with julius caesar and then mark antony; after their defeat by octavian, egypt became a roman province

people.name: augustus
people.about: ended the civil wars, kept the look of the republic while holding real power, and began the pax romana

people.name: jesus of nazareth
people.role: jewish teacher, central figure of christianity
people.about: preached love of god and neighbor and the coming kingdom of god; crucified under pontius pilate

people.name: paul of tarsus
people.about: spread christianity to non-jews around the eastern mediterranean; his letters are the oldest christian writings

people.name: cai lun
people.about: credited with improving papermaking using bark, hemp, and rags

people.name: zhang heng
people.about: built a water-powered model of the heavens and a device that detected distant earthquakes

people.name: galen
people.role: greek doctor in the roman empire
people.about: his many books on anatomy and medicine were followed in europe and the islamic world for more than a thousand years

people.name: constantine
people.about: the first christian emperor; ended persecution of christians and founded constantinople

people.name: ezana
people.about: converted to christianity and made aksum one of the first christian states

people.name: hypatia
people.about: taught mathematics, astronomy, and philosophy, and was murdered by a christian mob during a political feud

people.name: aryabhata
people.about: calculated pi closely, explained eclipses, and argued that the earth spins on its axis

people.name: justinian
people.about: reconquered much of the old western empire, built the hagia sophia, and gathered roman law into one code

people.name: muhammad
people.about: a merchant of mecca who, muslims believe, received the quran from god; he united arabia under islam

people.name: xuanzang
people.about: walked to india and back along the silk roads, brought home hundreds of buddhist texts, and spent the rest of his life translating them

people.name: wu zetian
people.about: the only woman to rule china as emperor in her own name; she expanded the exam system and backed buddhism

people.name: charlemagne
people.about: united much of western europe and encouraged learning; crowned emperor by the pope in 800

people.name: harun al-rashid
people.about: ruled from baghdad at the height of its wealth and learning; he appears in the stories of the thousand and one nights

people.name: al-khwarizmi
people.about: his book gave us the word algebra, and his name gave us the word algorithm

people.name: ibn al-haytham
people.about: his book of optics showed that we see because light enters the eye, and tested ideas by careful experiment

people.name: leif erikson
people.about: led the voyage that reached vinland, part of north america, about five centuries before columbus

people.name: murasaki shikibu
people.about: wrote the tale of genji, often called the world's first novel

people.name: ibn sina
people.about: known in europe as avicenna; his canon of medicine was a standard textbook for centuries

people.name: bi sheng
people.about: invented movable type made of baked clay, about four hundred years before gutenberg

people.name: william the conqueror
people.role: duke of normandy, king of england
people.about: won the battle of hastings in 1066 and ordered the domesday book survey

people.name: shen kuo
people.about: described the magnetic compass needle, movable type printing, fossils, and how landscapes are shaped by erosion

people.name: hildegard of bingen
people.about: wrote about medicine, plants, and her religious visions, and composed music that is still performed

people.name: eleanor of aquitaine
people.role: queen of france, then of england
people.about: one of the richest and most powerful women of medieval europe, and the mother of two english kings

people.name: jayavarman vii
people.about: built the bayon temple and the walled city of angkor thom, along with hospitals and rest houses across his kingdom

people.name: ibn rushd
people.role: philosopher and judge in muslim spain
people.about: known in europe as averroes; his commentaries on aristotle shaped both islamic and christian philosophy

people.name: saladin
people.about: united muslim lands against the crusaders and retook jerusalem in 1187; famed even among enemies for chivalry

people.name: maimonides
people.about: born in córdoba, he settled in cairo, served as a court physician, and wrote the guide for the perplexed

people.name: genghis khan
people.about: united the mongol tribes and launched conquests that created the largest land empire in history

people.name: rumi
people.about: his long poem the masnavi, about the soul's love for god, is still one of the most widely read books of poetry

people.name: kublai khan
people.about: grandson of genghis; conquered the song and founded the yuan dynasty

people.name: sundiata keita
people.about: his story is told in the epic of sundiata, still performed by west african griots

people.name: thomas aquinas
people.about: tried to show that christian faith and aristotle's reason could fit together

people.name: marco polo
people.about: his account of the court of kublai khan gave europeans a picture of asia

people.name: mansa musa
people.about: his lavish pilgrimage to mecca made mali famous; he built mosques and schools in timbuktu

people.name: ibn battuta
people.about: journeyed about 120,000 kilometers through the islamic world, india, china, and west africa

people.name: ibn khaldun
people.about: his muqaddimah tried to explain why dynasties rise and fall, an early work of social science

people.name: timur
people.about: built an empire from his capital at samarkand across persia and into india and anatolia, killing huge numbers of people

people.name: christine de pizan
people.about: one of the first women in europe to earn a living by writing; her book of the city of ladies answered attacks on women

people.name: zheng he
people.about: led seven huge treasure fleets across the indian ocean to arabia and east africa

people.name: sejong the great
people.about: had hangul, the korean alphabet, created so that ordinary people could learn to read and write

people.name: johannes gutenberg
people.about: developed movable metal type and the printing press in europe

people.name: joan of arc
people.role: french peasant girl and military leader
people.about: said voices told her to save france; she lifted the siege of orléans and was burned by the english

people.name: pachacuti
people.about: turned the kingdom of cusco into a great empire and likely built machu picchu

people.name: mehmed ii
people.about: conquered constantinople in 1453 and made it his capital

people.name: christopher columbus
people.about: reached the caribbean in 1492, opening lasting contact between europe and the americas; his rule there was brutal

people.name: leonardo da vinci
people.about: painted the mona lisa and the last supper and filled notebooks with studies of anatomy and machines

people.name: afonso i of kongo
people.about: became a catholic, modernized his kingdom, and wrote to the king of portugal protesting the slave trade

people.name: vasco da gama
people.about: the first european to reach india by sea

people.name: moctezuma ii
people.about: ruled the aztec empire at its height and died in spanish captivity

people.name: guru nanak
people.about: taught that there is one god, beyond hindu and muslim, and that all people are equal before god

people.name: nicolaus copernicus
people.about: argued that the earth and planets orbit the sun

people.name: michelangelo
people.about: carved david and painted the sistine chapel ceiling

people.name: ferdinand magellan
people.about: led the first expedition to sail around the world; he was killed in the philippines

people.name: babur
people.about: a descendant of timur and genghis khan who conquered northern india and wrote a frank memoir of his life

people.name: martin luther
people.about: his attack on indulgences began the protestant reformation; he translated the bible into german

people.name: bartolomé de las casas
people.about: after taking part in the conquest, he spent fifty years denouncing the cruelty of the colonists toward the peoples of the americas

people.name: hernán cortés
people.about: conquered the aztec empire with the help of tens of thousands of indigenous allies

people.name: suleiman the magnificent
people.about: expanded the empire, reformed its laws, and presided over its golden age

people.name: malintzin
people.about: also called la malinche; her skill with languages was crucial to cortés, and her role is still argued over in mexico

people.name: atahualpa
people.about: won a civil war against his brother, then was captured and executed by pizarro

people.name: elizabeth i
people.about: saw off the spanish armada; her reign was a golden age of english drama

people.name: akbar
people.about: expanded the empire across northern india and held debates between scholars of different faiths

people.name: tokugawa ieyasu
people.about: won the battle of sekigahara and founded the shogunate that ruled japan until 1868

people.name: yi sun-sin
people.about: defeated the japanese navy again and again with his turtle ships

people.name: galileo galilei
people.about: used the telescope to support copernicus and was forced by the church to take it back

people.name: william shakespeare
people.about: wrote hamlet, macbeth, romeo and juliet, and dozens more plays still performed around the world

people.name: johannes kepler
people.about: showed that the planets move around the sun in ellipses, not circles, and worked out the laws of their motion

people.name: queen nzinga
people.about: fought and negotiated with the portuguese for decades to keep her kingdoms in angola free

people.name: shah jahan
people.about: built the taj mahal in memory of his wife

people.name: aurangzeb
people.about: pushed the empire to its largest size, but his long wars and harsh religious policies left it weakened

people.name: john locke
people.about: argued that people have natural rights and that governments rule by the consent of the governed

people.name: isaac newton
people.about: described gravity and the laws of motion, and co-invented calculus

people.name: matsuo bashō
people.about: the greatest master of haiku, who wrote while walking across japan

people.name: sor juana inés de la cruz
people.about: one of the great writers of the spanish language, who defended the right of women to study

people.name: kangxi emperor
people.about: ruled for 61 years, expanded the empire, and sponsored huge dictionaries and encyclopedias

people.name: peter the great
people.about: modernized russia, built a navy, and founded st petersburg

people.name: voltaire
people.about: attacked religious intolerance and censorship with sharp wit

people.name: jean-jacques rousseau
people.about: wrote that legitimate government comes from the general will of the people

people.name: adam smith
people.about: the wealth of nations argued that free markets and division of labor create prosperity

people.name: james cook
people.about: mapped new zealand and the east coast of australia and crossed the pacific three times; he was killed in hawaii

people.name: catherine the great
people.about: expanded russia to the black sea, wrote to enlightenment thinkers, and tightened serfdom

people.name: george washington
people.about: led the continental army to victory and then stepped down after two terms

people.name: james watt
people.about: his improved steam engine powered the industrial revolution

people.name: tupac amaru ii
people.role: leader of an uprising in peru
people.about: claimed descent from the last inca rulers and led a great revolt against spanish rule; he was captured and executed

people.name: thomas jefferson
people.about: wrote the declaration of independence while enslaving more than 600 people over his life

people.name: toussaint louverture
people.about: a formerly enslaved man who led haiti's revolution; captured by napoleon's forces, he died in a french prison

people.name: olaudah equiano
people.about: his autobiography of enslavement and freedom helped turn british opinion against the slave trade

people.name: jean-jacques dessalines
people.about: led the final defeat of the french and declared haiti's independence in 1804

people.name: maximilien robespierre
people.about: led the reign of terror before he was himself guillotined

people.name: mary wollstonecraft
people.about: argued that women are not naturally inferior but only lack education

people.name: william wilberforce
people.about: led the campaign in parliament to end the slave trade

people.name: tecumseh
people.about: tried to unite native nations to stop american expansion, and died fighting alongside the british in the war of 1812

people.name: napoleon bonaparte
people.about: conquered most of europe, spread the napoleonic code, and was finally beaten at waterloo

people.name: ram mohan roy
people.about: campaigned against the burning of widows and for modern education, and is often called the father of the indian renaissance

people.name: simón bolívar
people.about: led the independence of venezuela, colombia, ecuador, peru, and bolivia

people.name: shaka
people.about: reorganized the zulu army and built a powerful kingdom in southern africa

people.name: abraham lincoln
people.role: sixteenth president of the united states
people.about: led the union through the civil war and moved to end slavery; assassinated in 1865

people.name: charles darwin
people.about: explained how species evolve by natural selection

people.name: john snow
people.about: traced a london cholera outbreak to one water pump, showing that the disease spreads through dirty water

people.name: hong xiuquan
people.about: believed he was the younger brother of jesus and founded a rebel kingdom in southern china

people.name: ada lovelace
people.about: wrote what is often called the first computer program, for charles babbage's analytical engine, and saw that such machines could do more than arithmetic

people.name: otto von bismarck
people.about: unified germany through three short wars and then kept the peace with a web of alliances

people.name: frederick douglass
people.about: escaped slavery and became one of the most powerful speakers against it

people.name: karl marx
people.about: argued that history is driven by class struggle and predicted a workers' revolution

people.name: florence nightingale

people.name: harriet tubman
people.about: escaped slavery and guided dozens of others to freedom on the underground railroad

people.name: louis pasteur

people.name: samori ture

people.name: sitting bull

people.name: cixi
people.about: the real power at the qing court for nearly fifty years

people.name: leopold ii
people.about: ran the congo as his private property through terror and forced labor

people.name: liliuokalani
people.about: was overthrown in 1893 by american businessmen backed by us marines; she also wrote the song aloha 'oe

people.name: menelik ii
people.about: defeated italy at adwa in 1896 and kept ethiopia independent

people.name: thomas edison
people.about: his laboratory produced the phonograph, a practical light bulb, and one of the first electric power stations

people.name: emperor meiji
people.about: reigned during japan's rapid transformation into a modern industrial power

people.name: emmeline pankhurst
people.about: led a militant campaign for women's right to vote

people.name: josé rizal
people.about: his novels exposed the abuses of spanish rule; his execution helped spark the philippine revolution

people.name: sun yat-sen
people.about: called the father of modern china; first president of the republic of china

people.name: marie curie
people.about: discovered polonium and radium and was the first person to win nobel prizes in two sciences

people.name: mahatma gandhi
people.about: led mass non-violent resistance against british rule; assassinated in 1948

people.name: vladimir lenin
people.about: led the bolshevik revolution and founded the soviet state

people.name: winston churchill
people.about: led britain through the second world war and refused to make peace with hitler

people.name: joseph stalin
people.about: industrialized the soviet union by force; millions died in his famines, purges, and labor camps

people.name: lise meitner
people.about: was the first to explain nuclear fission, with her nephew otto frisch, after fleeing nazi germany

people.name: albert einstein
people.about: developed the theories of relativity, changing our understanding of space, time, and gravity

people.name: emiliano zapata
people.about: fought for land for poor farmers under the slogan "land and liberty" and was assassinated

people.name: mustafa kemal atatürk
people.about: built a secular republic from the ruins of the ottoman empire

people.name: franklin d. roosevelt
people.about: led the country through the great depression and most of the second world war

people.name: benito mussolini
people.about: founded fascism and allied with hitler

people.name: adolf hitler
people.about: started the second world war in europe and ordered the holocaust

people.name: jawaharlal nehru
people.about: led india for its first seventeen years and helped found the non-aligned movement

people.name: ho chi minh
people.about: led the fight for vietnam's independence from france and then against the united states-backed south

people.name: haile selassie
people.about: appealed to the league of nations against the italian invasion, returned to power in 1941, and ruled until 1974

people.name: mao zedong
people.about: won the chinese civil war; his great leap forward and cultural revolution cost tens of millions of lives

people.name: sukarno
people.about: declared independence from the dutch in 1945 and led the new country for over twenty years

people.name: deng xiaoping
people.about: opened china's economy to markets, setting off decades of rapid growth

people.name: rachel carson
people.about: her book silent spring showed the damage done by pesticides and helped start the modern environmental movement

people.name: salvador allende
people.about: the first marxist elected president in latin america; he died during a military coup

people.name: kwame nkrumah
people.about: led ghana to independence in 1957 and championed african unity

people.name: alan turing
people.about: described the idea behind every modern computer and helped break german codes in the second world war

people.name: rosa parks
people.about: her refusal to give up her bus seat sparked the montgomery bus boycott

people.name: jonas salk
people.about: developed the first effective polio vaccine and chose not to patent it

people.name: norman borlaug
people.about: bred high-yield wheat that helped set off the green revolution; he won the nobel peace prize

people.name: indira gandhi
people.about: led india for sixteen years, including a period of emergency rule, and was assassinated by her bodyguards

people.name: nelson mandela
people.role: anti-apartheid leader and president of south africa
people.about: spent 27 years in prison, then led the country's peaceful move to democracy

people.name: eva perón
people.about: a champion of workers and the poor, she campaigned for women's right to vote, won in 1947

people.name: rosalind franklin
people.about: her x-ray images were key to discovering the structure of dna

people.name: fidel castro
people.about: took power in 1959 and ruled cuba as a communist state for nearly fifty years

people.name: anne frank
people.about: hid from the nazis in amsterdam for two years; her diary was published after she died in bergen-belsen

people.name: martin luther king jr.
people.about: led non-violent campaigns against segregation; won the nobel peace prize and was assassinated

people.name: neil armstrong
people.about: the first person to walk on the moon, in 1969

people.name: tu youyou
people.about: found artemisinin, a malaria drug, in an old herbal remedy; it has saved millions of lives

people.name: mikhail gorbachev
people.role: last leader of the soviet union
people.about: his reforms opened the soviet system and helped end the cold war peacefully

people.name: yuri gagarin
people.about: the first human in space, in 1961

people.name: eddie mabo
people.about: his court case ended the legal claim that australia had belonged to no one before british settlement

people.name: valentina tereshkova
people.about: became the first woman in space in 1963, orbiting the earth 48 times

people.name: wangari maathai
people.about: founded the green belt movement, which planted tens of millions of trees; first african woman to win the nobel peace prize

people.name: tim berners-lee
people.about: invented the world wide web

glossary.definition: the movement to end slavery and the slave trade.
a system in which a monarch holds total power, not limited by a parliament or written laws.
the change from hunting and gathering to farming, which happened on its own in several parts of the world after the last ice age. also called the neolithic revolution.
a writing system with a small set of letters that stand for individual sounds, rather than whole words or syllables.
an animal whose eggs have a waterproof membrane, letting them develop on dry land. reptiles, birds, and mammals are all amniotes.
the belief that animals, plants, rivers, and places have spirits. it is probably the oldest kind of religion.
a medicine that kills bacteria or stops them growing. the first, penicillin, was found in 1928.
the system of racial segregation and white minority rule enforced by law in south africa from 1948 to the early 1990s.
giving in to an aggressive power's demands in the hope of avoiding war, as britain and france did with hitler in the 1930s.
a channel or bridge built to carry water over long distances, especially the great stone ones built by the romans.
the study of the past through the things people left behind, such as tools, buildings, bones, and rubbish.
an agreement to stop fighting, which is not yet a full peace treaty.
a group of early human relatives from africa who walked upright but had brains about the size of a chimpanzee's.
the family of languages, and the seafaring peoples who speak them, that spread out of taiwan and across the pacific and indian oceans, from madagascar to easter island.
a name some historians give to the period when great thinkers in china, india, persia, israel, and greece laid the foundations of many later religions and philosophies.
the slow spread, over about three thousand years, of farmers speaking bantu languages from west-central africa across most of central, eastern, and southern africa.
the rapid expansion of the universe from an extremely hot and dense early state, about 13.8 billion years ago.
a written order to pay a sum of money at a later date or in another place. medieval merchants used them so they did not have to carry coins.
the radical wing of russia's marxist party, led by lenin, which seized power in 1917 and later became the communist party.
the period when bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, was the main metal for tools and weapons. it began at different times in different places.
the fall of several great civilizations of the eastern mediterranean and near east around 1200-1150 bce.
the religion founded on the teachings of siddhartha gautama, the buddha, about ending suffering through wisdom, ethics, and meditation.
a successor to muhammad as the political and religious leader of the muslim community. a caliph's state is a caliphate.
an economic system in which businesses and property are privately owned and goods are traded in markets for profit.
a group of traders traveling together, often with camels, for safety on long routes across deserts or mountains.
a system of hereditary social groups, especially in south asia, that shaped whom people could marry and what work they did.
the religion based on the life and teachings of jesus of nazareth, whom christians believe to be the son of god.
a city that rules itself and the land around it as an independent state, like athens or ur.
a complex society with cities, a government, specialized jobs, social classes, monumental building, and usually writing.
the long-term warming of the earth and the changes in weather that come with it, now driven mostly by burning fossil fuels.
money made as pieces of metal of fixed weight, stamped by a ruler or a city to guarantee their value. the first coins were made in lydia around 600 bce.
the long rivalry between the united states and the soviet union after the second world war, fought through arms races, spying, and wars in other countries rather than directly.
one country taking control of another land and its people, usually settling it or exploiting its resources.
the huge transfer of plants, animals, people, and diseases between the americas and the rest of the world after 1492.
the idea of a classless society where property is shared. in practice, the one-party states that followed marx and lenin.
the teachings of confucius and his followers about duty, respect, good government, and proper relationships between people.
a spanish or portuguese soldier and adventurer who took part in the conquest of the americas.
the catholic church's response to the protestant reformation, reforming itself and fighting protestantism.
a series of religious wars called by the popes, above all to take and hold jerusalem, from 1095 on.
the wedge-shaped writing pressed into clay tablets in mesopotamia, the oldest known writing system.
microbes that make food from sunlight and release oxygen. they changed earth's atmosphere billions of years ago.
a chinese tradition, linked to laozi, that teaches living simply and in harmony with the dao, the natural way of things.
the process by which colonies became independent countries, especially after 1945.
rule by the people, either directly (as in ancient athens) or through elected representatives.
a people living scattered far from their homeland who keep a shared identity, like the jewish, african, armenian, or indian diasporas.
the belief that kings get their authority directly from god and answer to no one on earth.
the molecule that carries the genetic instructions of living things. ancient dna lets scientists trace how people moved and mixed.
changing wild plants or animals over generations, by choosing which ones to breed, so that they depend on and serve humans.
a series of rulers from the same family.
a large state that rules over many different peoples and territories, usually gained by conquest.
an intellectual movement that stressed reason, science, and individual rights, and questioned the power of kings and churches.
a sudden outbreak of disease that spreads to many people in one area. one that spreads around the world is a pandemic.
the study of how diseases spread through populations, and how to stop them.
a living thing whose cells have a nucleus. all animals, plants, and fungi are eukaryotes.
the change in living things over many generations. charles darwin explained it by natural selection.
the dying out of a species. a mass extinction is when a large share of all species die out in a short time.
a far-right political movement that glorifies the nation and war, crushes opposition, and demands obedience to one leader.
an arc of good farmland in the middle east, from the persian gulf up through iraq and syria and down to the mediterranean coast, where farming first began.
a way of organizing medieval society in which land was granted in return for loyalty and military service, and peasants worked the land for lords.
coal, oil, and natural gas: the remains of ancient plants and sea life, which release energy and carbon dioxide when burned.
acts committed with the intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. the word was coined in 1944.
the complete set of dna in a living thing.
the idea, proven in the 1800s, that many diseases are caused by tiny living things such as bacteria and viruses.
"openness": gorbachev's policy of allowing more free discussion in the soviet union.
the growing connection of the world's economies, cultures, and peoples through trade, travel, and communication.
a system in which a country's money can be exchanged for a fixed amount of gold. most big economies used it from the 1870s until the 1930s.
the worldwide economic collapse that began with the 1929 wall street crash and lasted through most of the 1930s.
the rise of oxygen in earth's atmosphere about 2.4 billion years ago, caused by photosynthesizing microbes.
the spread, from the 1960s, of high-yield crops, fertilizers, and irrigation that greatly increased the world's food supply.
an association of craftworkers or merchants in a town that set rules, prices, and standards for its trade.
the korean alphabet, created in 1443 under king sejong, with letters whose shapes are based on how the mouth makes each sound.
the idea that the earth and the other planets go around the sun, set out by copernicus in 1543.
describing the blend of greek and near eastern culture that spread after the conquests of alexander the great.
the picture-based writing system of ancient egypt.
muhammad's move from mecca to medina in 622 ce, which marks the start of the islamic calendar.
the main religion of india, with roots in the vedas, many gods seen as forms of one reality, and belief in karma and rebirth.
the systematic murder of six million jews by nazi germany and its collaborators during the second world war.
the current geological epoch, which began when the last ice age ended about 11,700 years ago.
any member of the human family tree after it split from the line leading to chimpanzees, including extinct species.
a renaissance movement that studied greek and roman writings and focused on human abilities and life in this world.
people who live by hunting wild animals and gathering wild plants instead of farming.
a long period when the earth is cold enough for large ice sheets to cover parts of the continents. in everyday use, the last glacial period.
the policy of extending a country's power by taking over other lands, directly or through economic control.

work done under a contract that binds a worker to an employer for several years, often in return for the cost of the journey. after slavery ended, millions of indians and chinese went abroad this way.
in the medieval catholic church, a grant that reduced the punishment for sins, sometimes sold for money.
the shift from hand production to machines, factories, and fossil-fuel power, which began in britain in the late 1700s.
a general rise in prices, which means each unit of money buys less.
the period when iron became the main metal for tools and weapons, following the bronze age.
bringing water to fields through canals, ditches, or pipes.
the religion based on the quran, which muslims believe was revealed by god to the prophet muhammad.
the elite infantry of the ottoman empire, originally boys taken from christian families and trained as soldiers.
a business owned by many investors who each hold shares that can be bought and sold. the dutch and english east india companies were early examples.
the religion of the jewish people, based on the hebrew bible and one god's covenant with israel.
a political philosophy based on individual rights, elected government, the rule of law, and usually free markets.
the ability to read and write. for most of history only a small share of people had it.
a written sign that stands for a whole word or idea, like chinese characters, rather than a sound.
the charter english barons forced king john to accept in 1215, which put the king under the law.
the chinese idea that heaven grants the right to rule to a just ruler and takes it away from a bad one.
making large numbers of identical products, often on an assembly line.
a city with more than ten million people. there were two in 1950 and there are over thirty today.
the economic idea that a nation grows rich by exporting more than it imports and by using colonies as sources of raw materials.
the cultural region covering central and southern mexico and central america, home of the olmecs, maya, and aztecs.
the voyage across the atlantic that enslaved africans were forced to make, in brutal conditions.
people moving from one place to live in another, by choice or by force.
belief in a single god.
the seasonal winds of the indian ocean, blowing from the southwest in summer and the northeast in winter, which let sailors cross the ocean and back once a year.
printing with separate letters or characters that can be arranged, inked, printed, and used again. it was invented in china and later, separately, in europe.
preserving a dead body by drying it, as the egyptians did so the dead could live on in the afterlife.
the belief that people who share a language, culture, or history should have their own state, and loyalty to that nation.
the process by which living things better suited to their environment tend to survive and have more offspring, so their traits spread.
a species of human that lived in europe and western asia until about 40,000 years ago.
the "new stone age": the period of the first farming communities, still using stone tools.
people who move from place to place instead of settling, often with herds of animals.
animal bones and turtle shells used by shang kings to ask their ancestors questions; they carry the oldest chinese writing.
the "old stone age": the long period of human history before farming, when people lived as hunter-gatherers.
an outbreak of disease that spreads across many countries or the whole world.
a supercontinent that joined almost all of earth's land together, before breaking apart.
money printed on paper, first issued by the song government of china in 1024.
a writing material made in egypt from the stems of a water plant.
the division of a territory into separate states, especially the 1947 division of british india into india and pakistan.
the "roman peace": about two centuries of relative peace in the roman empire beginning with augustus.
"restructuring": gorbachev's program of reforms to the soviet economy and government.
the title of the kings of ancient egypt, who were seen as gods on earth.
the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria use sunlight to make food from water and carbon dioxide, releasing oxygen.
a journey to a holy place, such as mecca, jerusalem, rome, varanasi, or bodh gaya.
a large farm growing one crop for sale, like sugar, tobacco, or cotton, often worked by enslaved or forced labor.
the greek word for a city-state.
belief in many gods.
evidence from the time being studied, like a letter, a law, an inscription, or an object, as opposed to a later account of it.
the group of mammals that includes lemurs, monkeys, apes, and humans.
a machine for printing text from movable type, developed in europe by gutenberg around 1450; earlier printing existed in china and korea.
information, often biased or false, spread to win people over to a cause.
a member of the western christian churches that broke away from the roman catholic church during the reformation.
keeping people or goods apart for a time to stop a disease spreading. the word comes from the forty days ships had to wait at venice during plague years.
a method of dating once-living things up to about 50,000 years old by measuring how much radioactive carbon they still contain.
the religious movement begun by martin luther in 1517 that split western christianity into catholic and protestant churches.
a person forced to flee their country by war, persecution, or disaster.
the "rebirth" of art and learning based on classical models, which began in italy and spread across europe.
energy from sources that do not run out, such as sunlight, wind, flowing water, and the earth's heat.
payments a defeated country is made to pay for damage caused in a war.
a state without a monarch, ruled by elected officials.
the warrior class of pre-modern japan, who served lords called daimyo.
clean water, sewers, and the safe removal of waste, which have saved more lives than almost any medicine.
a province of the persian empire, run by a governor called a satrap.
finding out about the world by making observations, suggesting explanations, and testing them with experiments that others can repeat.
the change in how nature was studied, through observation, experiment, and mathematics, associated with copernicus, galileo, and newton.
the idea that government and public life should be separate from religion.
the forced separation of people by race in schools, housing, transport, and public places.
a peasant bound to work a lord's land who could not leave it without permission.
the military ruler of japan, who held the real power while the emperor was mostly a symbol.
the religion founded by guru nanak in the punjab around 1500, teaching devotion to one god and the equality of all people.
the network of overland trade routes linking china, central asia, india, the middle east, and the mediterranean.
a system in which people are owned as property and forced to work.
a deadly disease caused by a virus that killed hundreds of millions of people over history. it is the only human disease ever wiped out, in 1980.
a set of ideas holding that the community or state should own or control key parts of the economy and share wealth more equally.
a machine that burns fuel to boil water and uses the pressure of the steam to drive a piston. it powered the industrial revolution.
the vast grasslands of central eurasia, home to horse-riding nomads.
layered rock mounds built up by mats of microbes; some are among the oldest fossils on earth.
the right to vote.
the mystical side of islam, seeking a direct, personal experience of god through prayer, music, poetry, and dance.
the title of a muslim ruler, used by the ottomans, the delhi sultanate, and others.
the huge explosion of a dying star, which scatters heavy elements through space.
a writing system whose signs stand for syllables, like japanese kana or the cherokee script.
thousands of life-sized clay soldiers buried with qin shi huang, the first emperor of china.
a system in which the state tries to control every part of life, public and private.
fighting from long lines of dug-in ditches, which led to stalemate on the western front in the first world war.
the way imperial china managed relations with neighbors, who sent gifts and acknowledged the emperor in return for trade and recognition.
the growth of towns and cities, and the move of people from the countryside to live in them.
a medicine that trains the body's defenses to fight a disease before it strikes. the first, against smallpox, was made by edward jenner in 1796.
the oldest sacred texts of hinduism, composed in sanskrit and passed down orally for centuries.
a huge stepped temple tower of ancient mesopotamia.

topics.title: money and trade

topics.title: energy
topics.summary: every age of history has run on some source of power: muscle, fire, wind and water, coal, oil, the atom, and now the sun again.

topics.title: disease and medicine
topics.summary: plagues have killed more people than wars. this is the story of how they spread, and how people slowly learned to fight back.

topics.title: migration
topics.summary: humans have always been on the move: out of africa, across oceans, along the steppe, in chains, and in search of a better life.

topics.title: belief
topics.summary: from careful burials and painted caves to the great world religions and modern secular states: how people have answered the biggest questions.

topics.title: science
topics.summary: how many peoples, over thousands of years, built up a way of finding out how the world works by watching, measuring, and testing.

topics.title: cities
topics.summary: from the first walled towns to megacities of thirty million: why people crowd together, and what it has cost and given them.
